scope: Solver run of 2026-10-22 on MedicineBow (one NVIDIA RTX A6000): the five asynchronous cases of run_async_cases.py with v2 pictures and Gemma 4 12B, started from t = 0.1 s of a developed pimpleFoam run, 6000 steps of 5e-6 s; then eleven describe requests (run_live_sweep.py) at steps 500 to 5500, each with its own random window; and the records of a 600-step trial run (job 24757458).
notes: Sources are paths inside the archives named in 'archives'; solver-evidence-UM1RyJ.tar.gz is the run-archive.tar.gz that pack_run.py wrote at the end of the suite.
Files of kind gzip copy are gzip -9 copies (no name, mtime 0) of the named source; source_sha256 is the hash of the uncompressed bytes.

The describe request body is the same bytes in async-describe, async-server-error and async-timeout (same frame, same request); only the async-describe copy is here. The frames of async-no-llm (steps 3000, 3250, 3750) are byte-identical to those of async-sequence, and the frames of async-server-error and async-timeout (step 250) to that of async-describe, in all four files; they are not repeated here.
The sweep bodies are in the sweep archive; check-live.py compares the rebuilt bodies with the request_sha256 the client recorded for each body it sent.
The sweep archive leaves out python_svd_audit.npz (the POD audit file PODFoam writes at the end of every run, 120 MB per case) and the matplotlib cache; the suite archive has them.
Original records contain cluster paths and process ids as provenance.
